mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) above 4.5% over two consecutive months signals a restrictive monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and compressing equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the negative rank IC falls below 0.05.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) exceeding 2% signals weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate earnings expectations and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the subsequent 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 posts positive 60-day returns in more than 60% of triggered episodes, or the negative rank IC is not statistically significant at p < 0.01.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) above 6.5% for three consecutive months indicates deteriorating labor market conditions, reducing consumer spending and corporate margins, which in turn predicts negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of triggered periods, or the negative rank IC is not robust to a 5-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained contraction in industrial production (INDPRO) below its 12-month moving average by more than 3% for two consecutive months signals supply-side stress, which typically precedes negative equity returns as profit margins are squeezed over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO < 12-mo MA - 3% for two consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the negative rank IC is not significant at p < 0.05.

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent decline in both real personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) and housing starts (HOUST) for three consecutive months signals a broad-based weakening in demand, which is expected to drive negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 and HOUST both decline for three consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the interaction term's coefficient is not statistically significant at p < 0.10 in a multivariate regression.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp decline in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) below 2% combined with a concurrent rise in real savings (RSAFS) above its 5-year average signals an easing cycle with increased household savings, which typically precedes muted equity performance over the next 60 trading days due to lower consumption and investment.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are positive in more than 55% of triggered episodes, or the joint effect is not significant at p < 0.10 in a two-variable regression.

mechanism_narrative: A strong and persistent increase in payroll employment (PAYEMS) above its 12-month moving average by more than 1% for two consecutive months signals robust labor market expansion, which typically boosts consumer confidence and corporate earnings, predicting positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS > 12-mo MA + 1% for two consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are negative in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the positive rank IC is not significant at p < 0.05.

mechanism_narrative: A coordinated rise in both real personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) and housing starts (HOUST) above their respective 12-month moving averages for three consecutive months signals a broad-based demand recovery, which is expected to drive positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 > 12-mo MA AND HOUST > 12-mo MA for three consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are negative in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the interaction term is not significant at p < 0.10 in a multivariate regression.
